headword: {満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}
gloss: sold out; full house (with thanks to the audience)

definitions.gloss: sold out; full house; standing room only (with thanks)
definitions.explanation: An announcement that a venue is completely full, expressing gratitude to attendees. Originally from sumo and kabuki, where a banner with this phrase is displayed when all seats are filled.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{試合|しあい}は{満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}だ。
examples.english: Today's match is a full house.

examples.japanese: コンサートは{満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}で、チケットは{完売|かんばい}した。
examples.english: The concert was sold out — every ticket was gone.

examples.japanese: {大相撲|おおずもう}の{千秋楽|せんしゅうらく}は{満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}の{垂|た}れ{幕|まく}が{下|さ}がった。
examples.english: On the final day of the sumo tournament, the 'full house' banner was hung.

notes:
ORIGIN:
Literally means "full house — with thanks" ({満員|まんいん} = full capacity; {御礼|おんれい} = thanks, gratitude). Originally from the world of {大相撲|おおずもう} (grand sumo) and {歌舞伎|かぶき} (kabuki theater), where a special banner is displayed when all seats are sold.

USAGE:
Now used broadly for any event, concert, or venue that has sold out. It carries a celebratory tone — the organizers are publicly thanking the audience for filling the venue.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}の{垂|た}れ{幕|まく} (full-house banner)
- {満員御礼|まんいんおんれい}が{出|で}る (a full-house announcement is made)
